Umma · learner journey · build of 13 Nov 2026

Cook it tonight

A home cook has decided to make Gochujang Chicken Thighs for dinner. This is everything they see from stocking the pantry to the last plate, captured from the current main branch on an iPhone 16e simulator (iOS 26.2) with the mock AI. Screens follow your light or dark setting. Tap any screen to enlarge it.

  • Beginner to intermediate cook
  • iPhone, no glasses
  • Has most ingredients, not all
  • Hands full while cooking
6:05 pm

Tell Umma what's in the kitchen

Pantry starts empty. They tap the mic, say what they have (the simulator has no speech, so this run typed it), review what Umma heard, and confirm. Nothing lands in the pantry until they tap Confirm.

WorksEvery item is reviewed before it counts, and each row shows where it came from (Manual, confirmed today).

6:10 pm

Open the recipe

Gochujang Chicken Thighs from Umma Kitchen, version 2. Allergen notes sit above the ingredient list.

6:12 pm

Can I make it tonight?

Check my pantry compares the recipe with what they confirmed. Ingredients are split into Available, Uncertain, Missing and Optional, and each missing one has Find a swap and Add to pantry.

FrictionThey listed 7 things but the headline says “You’re missing 4 and check 4 items · 2 of 10 ingredients”. Soy sauce, honey and garlic were said without amounts, so they count as “check”. “Sesame oil” doesn’t match “toasted sesame oil”. Neutral oil and scallions are missing because nobody lists staples. The cook has almost everything, but the screen opens like a failing grade.

6:14 pm

Fill the gap with a swap

No rice vinegar. Find a swap offers apple cider vinegar (1:1 plus a pinch of sugar, medium confidence) and lemon juice (low confidence), with flavour, texture and the steps each one changes. Use this swap applies it for this cook only, and Undo swap reverses it.

FrictionThe vinegar swap carries a warning about pickling and canning. This recipe is a marinade, so the warning has nothing to do with it, yet it shows up on the swap card, in the fit summary, and as the yellow banner on step 1.

6:15 pm

Start cooking

Start cooking goes straight to step 1, with the swap already written into the instruction and an Adapted tag in the header. Big type, one step per screen. Notes, Repeat, Slower and Ask sit one tap away.

FrictionAsked “can I use apple cider vinegar here?”, the coach opens with a disclaimer about doneness and thermometers, then quotes step 1. It never mentions the swap they already chose. This is the mock coach, so real answers wait on Slice 4. Look is still marked “Coming with camera help”.

6:18 pm

Hands busy: timers

When a step has a duration, Umma offers a timer: Start or Skip. Running timers stay on screen as the cook moves through later steps, and the next step offers its own.

FrictionThe 20-minute marinade timer is labelled “Rest”, and it is still counting at the last step. Next lets the cook move straight past a wait, and once two timers run nothing says which step each one belongs to.

6:40 pm

Life interrupts

Pause holds the session on the server. The step and every timer are kept, and Resume picks up exactly where they left off.

WorksPausing never moves the step or resets anything, as the PRD requires.

6:50 pm

Finish the dish

Safety notes come in at the moment they matter: raw-poultry handling at step 2, a thermometer reading of 165°F at step 5. The last step shows Finish instead of Next.

WorksDoneness is never judged from color or a photo, and the warning says so plainly.

7:00 pm

Wrap up

“How did it go?” asks for Cooked it, Partly or Didn’t work, shows their swaps, and offers Save my changes so the apple cider vinegar version is ready next time. Done closes the session.

FrictionDone drops them back on Pantry fit, still showing the swap and a Start cooking button. Nothing confirms the cook was logged or that changes were saved. Also, the test tapped Save my changes and the toggle still read off. That may be how the test taps rather than an app bug, so it needs a manual check.

Captured by testCaptureCookTonightJourney (UmmaSmoke, opt-in with UMMA_JOURNEY_CAPTURE=1) against a local backend with seeded recipes. Clock times are illustrative. Timer readings are real but compressed, because the test moves through steps in seconds.
